headline: S&P fut +0.8%, Nasdaq fut +1.3%, Brent $107.6 on Russian fuel waiver, 10y 5.07%, Oct hold 85%
stance: Oil off on the Russian fuel waiver, futures up, AI credit unchanged. October hold 85%, December hike 90%: the Fed sits out until Oct 28 while chips set the 10y.

news.head: Nvidia +1.7% overnight on Samsung HBM base-die report
news.body: Report: Samsung will build the base die for Nvidia's next custom HBM on a 3nm process. Nvidia +1.7% (~3am ET). GTC Berlin Oct 20-22, keynote Wednesday.

news.head: CoreWeave -25% on the week, Oracle -9%; CDS 1,128bp, 300bp
news.body: CoreWeave 5y CDS +225bp on the week to 1,128bp Friday; 2031 bonds near 15%. Oracle 5y CDS +44bp on the week to 300bp.

news.head: Dai-ichi Life bids A$11.80 for Challenger, 19.8% premium
news.body: Non-binding, from a 20% holder; Challenger +19% Monday to an 8-year high, board reviewing. Also Monday: EQT takes Cleanaway private at A$6.94bn, +20%.

news.head: Apple iPhone Duo at $1,999: deliveries slip to January 2027
news.body: Preorders opened Oct 16; delivery estimates for the $1,999 foldable stretched to January 2027 within days.

implications: The waiver is a diesel story: 2.3m bbl this month against a crack at the 97th percentile. Brent still carries Hormuz: October is already the worst month for attacks since March.
October hold at 85% with PPI 6.3%: the Fed is letting the AI unwind tighten for it. If Nasdaq futures hold, the 10y gives back Friday's bid.

watch.head: No US data today; housing starts Tuesday, 8:30am
watch.body: Fed in blackout to the Oct 28 FOMC. Housing starts Tuesday, claims Thursday, Michigan final Friday.

watch.head: Netflix Tue; Meta, Tesla, IBM, TI Wed, after the close
watch.body: Meta needs $62.5bn revenue for its guide midpoint; 2026 capex guided $130-145bn. Netflix cut about 1,000 jobs last week.

watch.head: France: 10y 4.86%, Elderson today
watch.body: ECB's Elderson speaks today. 2027 budget in a split parliament; Paris banks -1% to -2% Monday (~6am ET).

watch.head: Hormuz: tanker mined Monday, 10 attacks last week
watch.body: Iranian officials say the oil pressure targets the Nov 3 midterms. Saudi intercepted a missile toward Yanbu Friday; East-West pipeline at 5.8m b/d.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Trump waived Graham Act penalties on Russian fuel: 2.3m bbl of diesel this month, 7.6m monthly after. Brent $107.6, -2% (~3:30am ET); WTI $99.5.
October hold odds 85% (~5am ET), December hike over 90%; blackout until the Oct 28 FOMC. 10y 5.07%, -3bp in Asia; 2y 4.72%.
France: 10y 4.86%, +10bp Monday after weekend riots; spread to Bunds widest since the euro crisis. Euro $1.120, near the 16-month low of $1.111.
sections.positioning: COT, Oct 13: wheat specs extended long at the 86th percentile, new this week. Wheat is the one grain where the fade has tested well.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: SOX -3.8% Friday, 8 straight down days, longest run since 2008; -11.4% on the week. Nasdaq 100 -5.5% on the week, S&P -1.1% Friday.
Futures (~5am ET): S&P +0.8%, Nasdaq 100 +1.3%; semis ETF +2.6% overnight. Kospi opened -3%, closed +0.5%; Nikkei -0.6% after a -2.3% low.
Jakarta -5.2% Monday to a 2020 low, -15% in two sessions on the MSCI standalone proposal. Europe: Stoxx 600 -0.7%, Paris -1.3%, banks -1.7% (~6am ET).
sections.positioning: COT, Oct 13: nothing new. Russell 2000 specs at the 99th percentile, third week; Nasdaq 100 at the 97th, fourth week. VIX shorts at the 6th, second week.

single_name.note: German American Bancorp: insider-buy rule fired, filing dated Oct 16, new to the list. Above its 200-day; days to cover 9.1. Long setup, score 3 of 5.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: HY data-center bonds average about 95 cents on par. A $5bn AI-cloud leveraged loan widened in syndication to above 11%, near the highs for AI infrastructure loans.
IG tech spreads about unchanged on the week; the widening sits in levered AI borrowers. A cut to junk forcing IG-only sellers is the next step down.
8-week bill demand at a record low last week, stop 4.05%, a one-year high. SOFR at or below the reserve rate most of the month: supply indigestion, not funding stress.
sections.positioning: Dealers' HY inventory at the 28th percentile of 3 years, mid-range, from the 99th in the prior week's data. Dealer paper is no longer the overhang.
